title: nautilus project manifest
description: A manifest-defined nautilus controller: tasks, tags by role, the server, and a configured field driver. Pure data — anything needing computation is generated upstream and committed. Secrets are NEVER in this file: NAUTILUS_TOKEN and NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD come from the environment.

name.description: The controller's name. Defaults to "nautilus"; also the default Sparkplug edge-node id and the default output name for `nautilus build`.

server.description: The tag API an HMI reads.

tasks.description: One program per scan. The FIRST task is the main task: it owns field I/O and is the default online-edit target.

tag-files.description: Files holding additional tags, each a bare YAML list of the same entries as `tags`. This is where a GENERATED tag set lives, so it stays a separate reviewable artifact instead of a 500-line smear through the file you edit — and how one project ships to several sites, by choosing which tag files a site's manifest composes. Read in order, then `tags` last. A tag declared twice in any two sources is an error: fix the generator, or narrow its scope.

tags.description: Tags declared by role. Hand-authored tags belong here; bulk or generated sets belong in a file listed under `tag-files`.

tag-meta.description: HMI documentation layered onto tags declared elsewhere, keyed by tag name or by a dotted field path (`P101.Speed`). Use it when a generator cannot supply documentation — `nautilus eip import` cannot, because Logix keeps tag descriptions in the offline project file. A generator that HAS descriptions should emit them into its tag file instead. This reaches only unit and desc: it can never change what the controller does.

driver.description: The field driver. Defaults to "memory", the loopback used for bring-up.

sparkplug.description: Republish the tag store as a Sparkplug B edge node.

retain.description: Persist operator state (setpoints, online edits) across restarts: a ConfigMap in a cluster, a JSON file anywhere else. An empty mapping takes both defaults.

file.description: JSON file path outside a cluster (default retain.json).

redundancy.description: Lease-based leader election: replicas elect one scanning leader, the rest stand by. Standalone (always leader) outside a cluster. An empty mapping takes the default lease name.

lease.description: coordination.k8s.io Lease name (default: the project name).

alarm-files.description: Files holding additional alarm definitions and rules, each a bare YAML list. Mirrors `tag-files:` exactly, and for the same reason: a GENERATED alarm set stays a separate reviewable artifact. Read in order, then `alarms:` last. An id declared twice in any two sources is an error naming both.

duration.description: A Go duration: "250ms", "2s", "1h30m". A bare number is not one — the unit is required.

addr.description: Listen address for the tag API (default "localhost:8080"). NAUTILUS_ADDR overrides at start.

online-edits.description: Allow a running controller's program to be replaced without a restart.

interval.description: How often the server pushes tag updates to connected clients.

historian.description: Base URL of a `nautilus historian` daemon; GET /api/history* proxies there. NAUTILUS_HISTORIAN_URL overrides.

hmi.description: A built HMI's directory, relative to the project (e.g. the SvelteKit `adapter-static` output, "./hmi/build") — must resolve inside the project, like every other manifest-referenced path. When set, the controller serves it at "/" (falling back to its index.html for a client-side route), and the built-in dashboard moves to "/_nautilus/". The HMI must call the tag API same-origin (a relative "/api/..." base URL).

task.description: One program on its own scan.

name.description: Identifies the task in status and acceptance tests. Defaults to the program's filename. "main" is reserved for the first task.

program.description: The program file in this project — normally .st, .fbd, .ld, or .sfc. The loader requires a PROGRAM declaration inside it, not a particular extension, so none is enforced here.

dt-tag.description: Tag to publish this task's measured scan delta into, for logic that integrates over real elapsed time.

tag.description: One tag, declared by the role it plays in the scan data path.

name.description: The tag name. ST binds it with VAR_EXTERNAL; the driver and HMI address it by this name.

role.description: input: driver → tag each scan, deliberately unseeded so a missing value faults loudly. output: tag → driver each scan; add init when the logic reads it back. setpoint: seeded operator/config value. state: seeded logic-owned value (latches, integrators).

type.description: A UDT declared by this project's ST, for a tag whose value is a struct — the same TYPE the programs bind with VAR_EXTERNAL, so the tag store and the logic cannot disagree about its shape. A typed setpoint or state needs no init: zero-of-type is its seed. A typed input stays unseeded, so a driver that has not delivered still faults loudly.

init.description: Initial value. A scalar for an untyped (or scalar-typed) tag. For a struct-typed tag (`type:`), init may instead be a mapping of member name to value — nested for a member that is itself a struct — to seed only the members that need a non-zero starting value; every member the mapping omits still takes the zero of its own field type. A struct-typed tag given a scalar init is an error. Required for setpoint and state unless `type` supplies one. On an output, needed only when the logic reads it before writing it (a seal-in latch).

unit.description: Engineering unit shown by an HMI ("°C", "%", "L/s").

desc.description: Human description shown in tag tables.

meta.description: Documentation for one tag or one field of a tag.

unit.description: Engineering unit shown by an HMI ("°C", "%", "L/s").

desc.description: Human description shown in tag tables.

type.description: memory: loopback for bring-up, so logic and HMI run before hardware exists. eip: polls an Allen-Bradley Logix controller. Custom buses are the Go tier.

manifest.description: eip: the imported tag manifest, generated by `nautilus eip import --format yaml`. Any path the project can read; no extension is enforced.

scan-rate.description: eip: default poll period for bound tags.

scan-classes.description: eip: named poll groups and their periods.

tag-classes.description: eip: glob patterns assigning tags to a scan class. Overrides the generated manifest, so imports stay regenerable and policy stays here.

sparkplug.description: Sparkplug B edge node. The MQTT password is NEVER here — set NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD.

broker.description: Broker URL, e.g. tcp://host:1883 or ssl://host:8883. Passed through to the MQTT client, which decides what it accepts, so no scheme is enforced here.

edge-node.description: Sparkplug edge node id. Defaults to the project name.

client-id.description: MQTT client id. Defaults to something derived from the edge node.

username.description: MQTT username. The password comes from NAUTILUS_MQTT_PASSWORD.

primary-host.description: Gate births on this SCADA host's STATE topic.

publish-interval.description: How often changed metrics are published.

device.description: Publish the field driver's input tags as a Sparkplug DEVICE with this id; its DBIRTH/DDEATH follow the driver's connection health. Empty means everything publishes at node level.

default-class.description: Report-by-exception tuning applied to metrics with no class.

metric-classes.description: Glob patterns assigning metrics to a named class.

min-interval.description: Never publish this metric more often than this.

max-interval.description: Publish at least this often even when unchanged.

every-change.description: Publish every transition unconditionally (alarms, counters) — deadband and min-interval are ignored.

alarms.description: Turn BOOL tags into ISA-18.2 alarm state: an active list, acknowledge, shelve, and an append-only journal behind /api/alarms. Rules cover the UDT members (a handful of them cover a whole fleet, because a fleet is the same types repeated); `defs` are the standalone BOOLs that name themselves. Omit the section entirely and the controller runs exactly as it did before alarms existed.

shelve-times.description: The shelf durations an operator screen offers, served on /api/meta. Default 5m 15m 30m 1h 2h 4h 8h.

notify.description: Where events go besides the journal. Notifiers run off the scan goroutine on a bounded queue: a slow endpoint drops events with a counter rather than stalling the scan.

rules.description: Generate definitions in bulk by matching a struct TYPE and member, or a tag glob. File order, FIRST MATCH WINS, materialized once at load.

defs.description: Explicit definitions, one per condition — the standalone BOOLs a rule cannot generalize.

site-from.description: Regexp over the TAG NAME whose first capture group becomes a definition's site, e.g. "^([A-Z]+[0-9]+)_" turns RTU9_WEL15_FIT_001 into site RTU9. Site is the alarm table's sort and filter axis and the `{site}` placeholder in a rule's templates. Omit it and site is empty.

area-from.description: The same, for area — the second axis, e.g. "^[A-Z]+[0-9]+_([A-Z]+[0-9]+)_".

alarm-defaults.description: What a definition gets when it does not say for itself. A value a rule or an entry spelled explicitly is never overwritten.

priority.description: Default priority. The package default is medium.

on-delay.description: How long the condition must hold before it annunciates — host-side qualification.

off-delay.description: How long it must stay clear before it returns to normal.

ack-required.description: false collapses unack-active to ack-active and unack-rtn to normal on arrival: annunciate-only, no operator workflow. Default true.

auto-clear.description: false means latched — clearing the field bit does not discharge the operator's obligation to see it. Default true.

shelve.description: Whether an operator may shelve it. Default true.

enable.description: A BOOL that must be true or the definition is Suppressed. Pointing it at a site's online flag is what stops a dead edge node from freezing four alarms on.

alarm-journal.description: The always-on in-memory ring, plus an optional durable sink. The ring sits in front of every sink, so the journal view works on a box with no database at all, and it is bounded by construction — the answer to a flapping storm.

sink.description: An additional durable journal. Omit it for the ring alone.

path.description: Where the `file` sink writes JSONL, inside the project. Rotated at a size cap.

dsn-env.description: The ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE holding the postgres sink's connection string — never the string itself, because a manifest is committed and a password in git is a password you have to rotate. Default NAUTILUS_ALARM_DB_URL, falling back to DATABASE_URL.

alarm-notify.description: One notifier: either `log: true` or `webhook: <url>`, never both in one entry.

log.description: Write every event to the structured log — often the only notifier a site needs, since a journal that also lands in the log stream is searchable by whatever already collects logs.

webhook.description: POST each event as JSON to this URL. Retries a couple of times, then drops rather than stalling the scan.

header.description: Header name for the webhook's API key (default Authorization).

header-env.description: Environment variable holding the webhook's API key. Same rule as the DSN: the secret is never in the file.

alarm-match.description: What a rule claims. All three are globs (*, ?, [class]); an empty field means any. A rule with no `member` matches only FLAT BOOL tags, and one with a `member` matches only struct members — a struct tag is not itself a BOOL, so "which member" is never a detail a rule can leave out.

type.description: The UDT name of a struct tag, as the project's ST declares it.

tag.description: A glob on the tag name.

alarm-rule.description: Generate definitions in bulk: name the (type, member) pair once and every matching tag gets an instance. First match wins across the rule list, and the expansion is materialized at load, never per scan — `nautilus alarms list` dumps the result so a few rules covering thousands of alarms stays auditable, not magic.

id.description: The definition's id. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Default "{path}".

name.description: The human-readable identity an operator reads. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Default "{desc} {member}".

site.description: Site. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Defaults to the tag's own, from `site-from`.

area.description: Area. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. Defaults to the tag's own, from `area-from`.

display.description: Display path. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces.

on-delay.description: How long the condition must hold before it annunciates.

off-delay.description: How long it must stay clear before it returns to normal.

enable.description: A BOOL that must be true, else Suppressed. Template over {tag} {member} {site} {area} {desc} {type} {path}; an unknown placeholder is an error, so a typo fails the load instead of reaching an operator screen as literal braces. e.g. "{site}__Online".

alarm.description: One alarm definition: the BOOL condition to watch and the operator policy that governs it.

id.description: The identity everywhere — row key, ack target, journal id. Defaults to `tag`.

tag.description: The condition PATH: a flat tag ("PumpFault") or one member of a struct tag ("FIT_001.HH"). Must resolve to a BOOL; true means in alarm. A path that does not resolve is Suppressed with a reason, never an error — one dark site must not fault the engine.

name.description: The human-readable identity. Defaults to the id.

on-delay.description: How long the condition must hold before it annunciates.

off-delay.description: How long it must stay clear before it returns to normal.

enable.description: A BOOL that must be true, else Suppressed.
